findings.section: A2 — one run of a case
findings.summary:
A Copilot session started 'as vloop run starts it' gets a preToolUse hook that runs os.Executable() with 'fence hook --phase

--root '. In this tool, os.Executable() is the agent-eval binary (a go run temp binary), which has no 'fence hook'. Every tool call of a real Copilot session would hit a failing hook. Tests with a fake copilot never run the hook, so the run passes and only the operator's acceptance fails.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/agent_copilot.go:136 exe, err := os.Executable(); :143 tail := " fence hook --phase " + phase + " --root "; os.Executable is used nowhere else in internal/ (grep). The Claude fences (fence/*.json) have no hooks, so only Copilot is affected.
findings.fix: Decide and pin how the hook resolves in the tool. Either agent-eval answers 'fence hook --phase --root' by calling the same judge 'vloop fence hook' runs, or the adapter gains a hook-command seam that the tool sets to 'vloop' on PATH, with vloop run's default (os.Executable) unchanged. Add a worked-example line or test: the hooks file of a tool-run Copilot session names a command that answers 'fence hook' with the judge's verdict.

findings.summary: A1 reads cases only from 'plugin/evals/', and no flag points elsewhere. The worked example's fixture lives 'in the tool's test data, not under plugin/evals/', yet '--case fixture-*' must find it. The brief does not say how. Also, the Claude line reuses '--out <tmp>/o', which the line before says exits 2 because it is not empty.
findings.evidence: Brief A1: 'The cases are the directories of plugin/evals/ ... in name order'. Worked example: 'A fixture case (in the tool's test data, not under plugin/evals/)'. tools/release/main.go:23 run(args, dir, stdout, stderr) takes a dir, so a test could pass a temp root, but the brief never says the cases are read relative to it.
findings.fix: State that the cases are '<dir>/plugin/evals/', where dir is the directory run is given (the repository root under go run). Tests build a temp root holding plugin/evals/fixture-review/ and plugin/evals/operate-fixture/. Give the Claude line its own --out.

findings.summary: Several values a gate will compare are described, not written. Only 'unknown agent nope' is literal. The <reason> texts for a missing flag, --runs below 1, a bad duration and a non-empty --out are not pinned, and the worked example's non-empty --out line pins no message. Also unpinned: what happens when no case matches --case; whether report.json's mean is rounded (the worked example says 0.67, the computed value is 0.666…); the table's column widths and separators, the NOTES separator for several failed graders, whether <n> in the total counts all cases or only scored ones, and the $ precision; whether cost_usd includes the judge's calls.
findings.evidence: Brief A1: 'prints agent-eval: <reason> on stderr and exits 2'. A5: '<n> case(s) · <s> skipped · <e> error(s) · $<cost>'. Worked example: 'mean 0.67' against weights 1,2,1,2 with b=0, which gives 4/6.
findings.fix: Write each reason literally (e.g. 'agent-eval: --model is required', 'agent-eval: --out <dir> is not empty'), decide 'no case matches' (exit 2 with a literal message, or exit 0 with an empty table), say report.json keeps full precision and the table rounds to 2 decimals, give one literal stdout line in the worked example, and say whether judge cost is counted.

findings.summary: A run can end in error ('scaffold exited <code>', 'no session result'), but run objects have no status or reason field. The case status is undefined when, at --runs 3, some runs score and some error.
findings.evidence: A5 run object: {score, graders, cost_usd, credits, wall_ms}. Case: status scored|skipped|error and 'mean ... over the scored runs', which implies mixed runs exist.
findings.fix: Add 'status' and 'reason' to each run. Pin that a case is 'error' when any run is, with the first error's reason, and that mean is taken over the scored runs.

findings.section: A2 / Violations the review must rule on
findings.summary: Runner.Run discards stdout after Parse, and Args hard-codes '--output-format json'. The tool cannot keep a transcript or stream Claude without a new seam in internal/driver. 'Unchanged: vloop run's sessions' and the violation 'any change to the argv, record or output of a vloop run session' can be read as forbidding any edit to internal/driver, so a careful planner may stall or a reviewer may fail a correct task.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/session.go: Args ends with "--output-format", "json"; Run parses stdout.Bytes() and keeps only the record.
findings.fix: Say explicitly that internal/driver may gain an exported seam (stdout handed to the caller, output format chosen by the caller) as long as vloop run's argv, records and existing session tests stay unchanged.

findings.summary: Unsure. Several event shapes have no source in the repository: Copilot's assistant.message data.content and tool.execution_complete data.result.content, and Claude's stream-json assistant/tool_use/tool_result layout. The repository guideline says an external tool's format comes from the tool or its docs. Fixtures written from the brief will pass whatever shape the brief states, so a wrong field only shows at acceptance.
findings.evidence: Confirmed in the repo: toolCallId and toolName (internal/driver/agent_copilot_parse_test.go:76-81), data.arguments and assistant.message (tools/copilot-acceptance/hook.py:122, run.sh:112). No hit for data.result.content, data.content or a stream-json transcript (grep over the repo). .vloop/repo-guidelines.md, first lesson.
findings.fix: Before the run, have the operator capture one real transcript per agent, commit them as the tool's testdata, and cite them (plus tools/copilot-acceptance/hook.py) as binding. The A3 field names then come from the captures.

findings.section: A2 — one run of a case
findings.summary: 'a phase vloop run starts (... review-brief)' is half right. vloop brief review starts review-brief sessions, not vloop run. The '<agent> does not run <phase>' skip cannot happen today: both adapters support all seven phases, so no test can reach it.
findings.evidence: internal/driver/agent.go:110-115 (claude Supports) and internal/driver/agent_copilot.go:74-76 (copilot Supports) list plan, work, review, second-review, gate-review, verify and review-brief. 'vloop brief --help' lists 'review  Review a brief in a fresh session'.
findings.fix: Say 'a phase vloop starts', and note that the unsupported-phase skip is defensive and has no reachable case with today's adapters (or cover it with a fake adapter).

findings.summary: The sentence that defers the runner is not the closing sentence of docs/design-notes/multi-agent-backends.md. The note ends one paragraph later.
findings.evidence: docs/design-notes/multi-agent-backends.md:94-96 'A backend-agnostic eval runner is deferred: ... needs it first.'; :97 'The fence audit is worth doing even if no other model is ever added.' (the file's last line).
findings.fix: Write: 'the sentence ending "needs it first." gains: It is tools/agent-eval since B33.'

findings.summary: No domain invariant is cited. The tool starts sessions, and S-1, S-2 and S-4 govern them. This repository's architect skill asks briefs to cite the invariants that apply by ID.
findings.fix: Add '- docs/domain/domain-model.md — S-1, S-2 and S-4: the sessions the tool starts are the same sessions, in a scratch workspace'.

decisions: A repository tool, not a vloop subcommand: sound, since plugin/evals/ is not extracted (internal/driver/extract.go skips evals).

Sessions start under the phase's fence; the case's allowed_tools and max_turns are ignored: sound, but the scores are not comparable with claude plugin eval's results, which the brief already accepts.
Claude streams only in this tool: sound.

The judge is always Claude, default sonnet, three votes with the majority deciding: fine. The basis ('as claude plugin eval's reports show its judge voting') is not in the repository and I could not run claude plugin eval --help to check it.
--case uses path.Match and is repeatable: fine. The claim that claude plugin eval --help offers this glob is unverified for the same reason.
Cases of skills with no phase (operate, create-brief) are skipped, not failed: sound.
The Copilot-to-Claude tool-name table: it covers every name internal/fence/judge.go:107-133 knows; fine.

The qualifying rule (3 runs, every case of the phase at a mean no lower than the phase's default Claude model on the same tool): consider a tolerance or 'no case drops a grader Claude passes'. Three runs of llm-graded cases are noisy, so 'no lower' will flip on a single vote. The rule also needs a Claude baseline run per phase, which costs money.
Defaults: --timeout 20m, --out must be absent or empty, --runs 1: fine.
Acceptance records the scores on #84 (the terra replacement issue) as well as in copilot-cli-experiments.md: consistent with B32; the operator posts it.
checked: facts (adapters, Runner/Args, extract, fence hooks, judge tool names, every case's prompt.md and grader frontmatter, release tool shape, design notes), consistency (worked-example arithmetic, contract vs example), rules (CLAUDE.md, guidelines, architect additions), runnability (go check after each task, gates vs fakes, acceptance)
